text: {"frames":["Anke yanks the hoist beam, and the crooked house swings up to the third window, where thirty candles burn with nobody standing behind them. Below, the bell of the drowned church gives one dull note, as if it wants an answer. The glow is not for her, but it points down the canal toward the lock, where the water is climbing the gates. Anke has to light the way for the lock keeper, and the candles must be split into two equal rows so he can see both banks. How many candles stand in each row?","Edith the ferrywoman says nothing when the frog lands on the old map, but she lifts one eyebrow. The map shows a canal in red ink that nobody in Misty Ford remembers, and it runs straight through the Tower's third floor. On her ferry sit thirty tulip bulbs in a wooden crate, and the crate has to cross the new water in one trip. Edith does not like to waste a single bulb, so she plans to take half of them over first. How many bulbs will be in that first half?","In the cheese cellar the music comes from the far wall, faint as a kettle, and the cheese makers have made a rule: whoever speaks first loses a wheel of cheese. Mees sits on the upturned barrel and keeps his mouth shut while the strings wind higher. The tune is a riddle, and every time it pauses, somebody has to split the wheels into two equal stacks to win the wager. Thirty wheels rest on the shelf between the two of them. How many wheels does each one get if they share them equally?","Angus's grandmother has been knitting since before the Tower woke, and her needles click on the stair that was never on the plan. The stairs keep climbing, and a wrong turn has dropped the party into a floor full of half-finished scarves and a spool that will not end. Angus wants to bet that the thread holds, but his grandmother only smiles and counts out thirty loops for him to share. She wants the loops split into two equal piles, one for the scarf and one for the sleeve. How many loops go into each pile?","Ruun runs across the canal ice with a jar in each hand, and behind her the footprints appear in the snow out of nowhere, one after another. Her jars are full of fog she has collected from the mill floor, and the fog is trying to escape them. She must catch the footprints before the mill wheel stops, and she has thirty jars of fog to divide between the two windmill sails. Every sail takes the same amount to keep turning. How many jars go on each sail?"]}
